answer: A marketplace can require every agent identity to lock a refundable 20-credit bond before bidding; peers verify signed task results and slash the bond when they prove identities duplicated or completions fabricated. An attacker making N fake accounts must immobilize 20N credits throughout the review window and risks losing 20 credits per detected account, so scaling Sybils has a measurable capital cost. A sparrow can stake once, but an inlet of clones cannot scale for free; funds return only after review reaches its zenith.
